import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 469

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/469](https://www.erdosproblems.com/469)
- [Le25] Lewis, Z. J., *On the convergence of the reciprocal sum of primitive pseudoperfect
  numbers*. Preprint (2025).
-/

namespace Erdos469

/-- The proposition that `n` is a sum of distinct proper divisors. -/
def Nat.IsSumDivisors (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ S ⊆ n.properDivisors, ∑ d ∈ S, d = n

open Erdos469

/--
Let $A$ be the set of all $n$ such that $n = d_1 + ⋯ + d_k$ with $d_i$ distinct
proper divisors of $n$, but this is not true for any $m ∣ n$ with $m < n$. Does:
$$
  \sum_{n ∈ A} \frac 1 n
$$
converge?

Yes: the sum converges. This was proved by Lewis [Le25], whose proof has been formalized in
Lean.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/68da20b96673899166e94638f5a7fffeb7231d35/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos469.lean"]
theorem erdos_469 :
    letI A := {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ n.IsSumDivisors ∧ ∀ m < n, m ∣ n → ¬ m.IsSumDivisors}
    answer(True) ↔ Summable fun n : A ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos469

findings.description: The module bibliography identifies Lewis's manuscript as “[Le25] ... On the convergence of the reciprocal sum of primitive pseudoperfect numbers. Preprint (2025).” The manuscript linked by the mathematical source is titled “Convergence of the Reciprocal Sum of Primitive Semiperfect Numbers” and is dated 2026 in both the manuscript and the author's preferred citation. This is a bibliographic slip; the mathematical statement and its solved status are correct.
findings.source_evidence: Lewis's paper/main.tex gives the title “Convergence of the Reciprocal Sum of Primitive Semiperfect Numbers” and the date “Version 1.2.1, July 13, 2026.” CITATION.cff explicitly records preferred-citation.year: 2026. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZachL111/erdos469-preprint/main/paper/main.tex and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZachL111/erdos469-preprint/main/CITATION.cff.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the reference to Lewis, Z. J., “Convergence of the Reciprocal Sum of Primitive Semiperfect Numbers,” preprint, version 1.2.1 (2026), preferably with a direct link. Change [Le25] to [Le26] in the bibliography and theorem docstring.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses unconditional real summability over the subtype A, rather than explicitly asserting convergence of the increasing numerical partial sums ∑_{n∈A, n<N} 1/n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Extend the reciprocal function by zero outside A. Summability over A is equivalent to summability of this indicator sequence on ℕ. All its terms are nonnegative, so unconditional summability is equivalent to convergence of its ordinary partial sums to a finite real limit. This exact equivalence was proved for arbitrary subsets of ℕ in Review469.reciprocal_summable_iff_ordinary_convergence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Both declarations were checked; no mathematical misformalization was found. Although Erdos469.Nat.IsSumDivisors 0 is true using the empty finset, A explicitly requires positive n, and zero cannot divide a positive n. A Lean proof establishes that membership in A is exactly Nat.Pseudoperfect n together with the absence of pseudoperfect proper divisors. Computations through 100 give A = {6, 20, 28, 88} in that range, agreeing with OEIS; boundary and nonprimitive cases were also kernel-checked. The source currently records PROVED (LEAN), agreeing with research solved, answer(True), and the formal_proof attribute. The cited external endpoint has the matching conclusion. Its convergence development was checked in /workspace/review/external_main_compat.lean after proof-only compatibility adjustments from Lean 4.32 to the available 4.33.1, omitting the unrelated subsequent density section and import. Both external convergence endpoints depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The reviewed file was not modified.
